usual_baseline: Overuse, not underuse. Cycle 1 finds antibiotics given in 50–88% of repairs, including low-risk ones. Guideline compliance runs 27–53%. High-risk mesh patients often get the wrong regimen: only 1 of 23 in one unit, 6 of 22 in another.
fix_that_works: Written high-risk criteria plus teaching cut antibiotic use from 87.8% to 48.1% with no rise in complications [2726]. Presenting results with posters raised compliance from 27.1% to 80% in ventral repair [2859] and to 84.6% in groin repair [2861], but re-audits covered one month and 13–15 patients.
fix_that_fails: No failed fix reported in these audits. Low-risk patients still got unneeded antibiotics after teaching: 2 of 4 [2859] and 1 of 2 [2861].
consultant_advice: A useful stewardship audit, but most units report the same overuse. Re-audit with enough patients and a longer period than one month. Measure the right drug and timing for high-risk mesh repairs, and record wound infection, as one audit did (1.04%) [2513].
